findings.summary: The client told one rotation refusal from another by matching the server's message text, because errorCodeFromStatus collapsed three distinct 409s into one 'conflict' code and left nothing else to branch on. Rewording a sentence would have changed the client's behaviour silently; worse, the matcher was already wrong for three of the five refusals, since version-taken, copies-do-not-match and history-not-allowed all fell through to key-is-current. Each refusal now carries its own reason via RespondErrorCoded and the client maps code to meaning, with the message kept for display only.

control.observed: With the prose matcher restored, six tests fail and six pass. Three failures read 'expected key-is-current to be version-taken / copies-do-not-match / history-not-allowed', which is the collapse itself; the reworded-message case and the unknown-code case fail too. Real assertion failures, and the suite still builds.
